role.altitude: The planner keeps designing plans, advising officials and holding public meetings; collecting data, writing standard rules and sorting reactions shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping data loads, rule libraries and map templates current
role.ambitious_version: A planner who publishes the land use monitor every quarter instead of once a year and reads every reaction with themes already grouped.

tasks.short: Gather goals, plans and background studies, design plan or policy options and rules, agree them with other departments, write the council proposal, get it adopted, publish it and promote it to the public.

steps.what: Urban planner gathers council goals, existing plans and rules, and background studies on environment, traffic and housing

loop.input: The background studies for the plan area (environment, noise, traffic, water) and the planner's list of topics.
loop.output: A list of constraints and limit values per topic, each with the report name and page.
loop.check: Every constraint must quote a passage found on the cited page, or it is dropped; reports the step cannot read are listed; the planner reads the cited pages before using a constraint.
loop.why_not_simpler: Background studies are free-text reports with limits stated in prose and tables in different places.

steps.what: Urban planner designs plan or policy options and the map
Urban planner writes the land use and zoning rules, taking standard wording from the rule library
Urban planner agrees the draft with traffic, environment, housing and utility colleagues
Urban planner writes the council proposal and the explanatory memorandum

loop.input: The agreed plan rules with their ids, the constraint list with page references, and the memorandum template.
loop.output: Draft memorandum sections explaining each rule and the constraints behind it.
loop.check: Every rule reference must resolve to a rule id in the plan and every study reference to a listed page, or the sentence is marked; the planner edits every section and writes the choices made.
loop.stop: One draft per plan version; if rejected, the planner writes the section.
loop.why_not_simpler: The template gives the chapters; explaining why each rule is there needs prose.

steps.what: Municipal council debates and adopts the final plan
Urban planner publishes the adopted plan on the national planning portal and in the official gazette
Urban planner promotes the plan at information sessions and answers questions from residents and developers

approvals.approved_version: plan rules and map exactly as adopted by the council in s6; the published files are that version and any change needs a new decision

tasks.design: A bounded step pre-reads background studies and lists constraints with page references for the planner to check. Standard rule wording comes from a rule library in the plan software ({OTHER}), so the planner writes only the area-specific rules; a bounded step drafts the explanatory memorandum with every rule and study reference resolved. Agreeing with colleagues, the council decision and public sessions stay with people; the adopted files are published through the planning portal's standard upload ({GOV_PORTAL}), which checks the format.
tasks.previous_blocker: Background studies were read in full for each plan, and standard rules were copied from earlier plans by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Plan software holds standard rule wording; language models can pre-read reports with checkable page references.
tasks.still_hard: Weighing housing, traffic and environment against each other, and getting departments and the council to agree.
tasks.human_edge: Designing a plan that politicians, residents and developers can accept.
tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time on boilerplate and more on design and talks; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Which limit values planners miss when studies state them only in prose.

evidence.claim: Language models can pre-read long reports and list stated limits with page references that can be checked.
Plans must be adopted by the council and published in a standard digital form; national planning law sets the details.

assumptions: Boundary: from gathering goals and studies to the plan published and explained; objections and appeals are outside.
Input contract for s1: background studies delivered as readable PDF or text by the consultants who write them; fallback is reading in full.
Input contract for s3: a rule library with standard clauses kept by the planning team; about half of a typical plan's rules are standard clauses.
The council's decision and the talks with colleagues and the public do not change.
unknowns: How many plans and policy revisions the planner handles per year.
Whether the municipality keeps a rule library today.
research_questions: How often does the pre-read miss a limit the planner later finds?
How much drafted memorandum text survives the planner's edit?

already_counted.description: Urban planner reads the cited pages of listed constraints.
Urban planner edits drafted memorandum sections.

incremental.description: Urban planner keeps the rule library current when national rules change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a new policy area with few standard rules and little background study; high: a routine plan revision with several background studies and mostly standard rules.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the project proposal, check it against the zoning rules, assess feasibility and cost, consult colleagues on impacts, write advice with alternatives and explain it to officials.

steps.what: Urban planner reads the developer's project proposal and notes its key figures

loop.input: The project proposal documents and drawings' text.
loop.output: A table of key figures: floor area, height, dwellings by type, parking places, uses, each with the page where it is stated.
loop.check: Every figure must appear on the cited page, or the cell is left empty; totals are recomputed from the parts; the planner checks each figure against the drawings.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals come as free-form documents; there is no fixed form to read the figures from.

steps.what: Urban planner checks regulatory conformance of the proposal with the zoning plan and rules for the location
Urban planner makes a rough land development calculation on the standard sheet
Urban planner assesses feasibility and cost-effectiveness of the project
Urban planner consults traffic, environment and housing colleagues on impacts and possible alternatives
Urban planner writes the advice memo on feasibility, conformance and alternatives

loop.input: The conformance check results per rule, the feasibility estimate table and the advice template.
loop.output: A draft conformance section listing each rule, the proposal's value and whether it fits.
loop.check: Every rule cited must resolve to a rule id for the location and every value to the project figures table, or the line is marked; the planner writes the feasibility judgement and alternatives and edits the rest.
loop.why_not_simpler: The check gives a table; officials need it in a few sentences per issue.

steps.what: Urban planner advises planning officials on the project in a meeting and answers their questions

tasks.design: A bounded step reads the developer's proposal into a table of key figures with page references for the planner to check against the drawings. Where the location's rules are available as structured values on the planning portal ({GOV_PORTAL}), a rule check compares each figure with its limit and lists conflicts; a standard land development sheet gives the rough cost. Consulting colleagues, judging feasibility and alternatives, and advising officials stay with the planner; a bounded step drafts only the conformance section of the memo.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rules were looked up per parcel in long plan texts, and proposal figures were copied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Planning portals publish rules per location, many with structured values; language models can pull figures from documents with page references.
tasks.still_hard: Rules written as open norms ('good spatial planning') need judgement, not a check.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a better alternative for the site and explaining it to officials.
tasks.altitude: The planner spends advice time on alternatives instead of lookup; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Which rules can be checked as values and which stay open norms.

evidence.claim: Language models can extract stated figures from documents with page references, so each can be checked.
Zoning rules and checklists can be configured as value checks where the rule states a number.

assumptions: Boundary: from the project proposal to officials advised; the decision and any permit are outside.
Input contract for s2: rule values per location from the planning portal, published by the municipality's own plan; project figures from s1 checked by the planner; fallback is reading the plan text.
Coverage: about 60% of the rules that apply to a typical project have structured values; s2 is priced at that share and open norms are judged by hand.
Talks with colleagues and officials do not change.
unknowns: How many project proposals reach the planner per month.
How much of the local plan is published with structured values.
research_questions: How many conflicts does the rule check find that the planner would have missed, and the reverse?
How long do officials take to decide after receiving the memo?

already_counted.description: Urban planner checks extracted figures against the drawings.
Urban planner reviews the rule check and judges open norms.

incremental.description: Urban planner updates the rule check when the plan or national rules change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a complex project outside the current plan, judged mostly on open norms; high: a routine infill project within a plan with structured rule values.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define the question, collect land use and population data, prepare it, make maps with overlays, write the report, get it approved and publish it.

steps.what: Urban planner defines the question and the maps and figures the report needs
Urban planner collects land use, building and population data from registers and statistics downloads
Urban planner joins and cleans the data and calculates figures such as population density per area
Urban planner creates land area maps overlaid with variables such as population density in the GIS
Urban planner writes the narrative report around the maps and tables

loop.input: The analysis tables, map titles and legends, and the report template.
loop.output: Draft descriptive paragraphs per map and table; the interpretation and conclusions are written by the planner.
loop.check: Every number in the text must match a cell in the analysis tables, or it is marked; no source or reference may be added that is not in the data list; the planner edits every paragraph.
loop.stop: One draft per table version; if rejected, the planner writes the paragraph.
loop.why_not_simpler: The template places maps and tables; describing what they show takes sentences.

steps.what: Planning team lead reviews the final report and approves it for publication
Urban planner publishes the report on the municipal website

approvals.approved_version: land use report, final version approved in s6; any edit after approval voids it

tasks.design: Scheduled loads on the {DATA_PLATFORM} pull the land use, building register and population statistics the planning team uses, and versioned scripts join them and compute figures such as density per area. Map templates in the GIS ({OTHER}) apply the house style to overlays, and a bounded step drafts descriptive paragraphs with every number checked against the tables. The planner defines the question, interprets the maps and writes conclusions; the team lead approves the final version before the planner publishes it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each report started with downloads and spreadsheet joins, so recurring monitors took as long as new reports.
tasks.enabler_now: Registers and statistics offices publish open data by area; scripts and map templates make repeats cheap.
tasks.still_hard: New questions need new data and new scripts; the first run saves little.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing which pattern on the map matters for the plan.

ambition.what: Publish the land use monitor every quarter instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends report time on what the maps mean; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Which data loads break when registers change their format.

evidence.claim: Scripts on a governed data store can load open register and statistics data by area and recompute figures on each run.
A consultancy partly refunded a government report that contained fabricated references, which is why drafted text may add no source.
Text made with AI to inform the public must be disclosed unless a person edits it under responsibility.

assumptions: Boundary: from the report question to the report published; decisions based on it are outside.
Input contract for s2: land use and building data from the national registers, population per area from the statistics office, loaded on a schedule by the data platform; fallback is manual download.
Coverage: about 60% of reports are recurring monitors on already loaded sources; s2 and s3 are priced at that share, and new questions still need manual collection and new scripts.
The team lead's review and the planner's interpretation do not change.
unknowns: How many land use reports per year are recurring.
Whether a GIS specialist or the planner makes the maps today.
research_questions: How long does a recurring monitor take after the first scripted run?
How many numbers in drafted paragraphs are marked?

already_counted.description: Urban planner checks data loads and script results.

incremental.description: Urban planner maintains scripts and data loads when sources change.
Urban planner keeps map templates current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a one-off report on a new question with data not yet loaded; high: the yearly land use monitor repeated on the same sources.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare public meetings, write and send invitations, hold the meeting with officials, experts, developers and residents, report the views raised, process written reactions and follow up on issues.

steps.what: Urban planner prepares the public meeting: participants, venue, presentation and maps
Urban planner writes the invitation and the public notice
Urban planner sends the invitations to stakeholders and residents of the area and posts the notice
Urban planner holds the public meeting with officials, experts, developers, residents and interest groups to address the land use issues
Urban planner writes the meeting report with the views and questions raised and the answers given

loop.input: The transcript of the meeting recording and the planner's own notes.
loop.output: Draft report: views and questions grouped by theme, each with the answer given in the meeting.
loop.check: Every view must cite a transcript time or a line in the planner's notes, or it is dropped; speakers are named only as their role; the planner listens to cited passages where the summary is unclear and edits the report.
loop.why_not_simpler: A transcript is hours of free speech; a template gives the report headings, not the views.

steps.what: Urban planner reads and sorts written reactions received after the meeting

loop.input: Each written reaction and the theme list from the meeting report.
loop.output: Each reaction tagged with one or more themes and the quoted sentence behind each tag.
loop.check: Every tag must quote a sentence found in the reaction; reactions with no tag go to a 'read first' list; the planner reads every reaction in full before answering.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reactions are free letters and e-mails; keywords miss views stated in other words.

steps.what: Urban planner follows up with officials and interest groups on the issues raised

approvals.approved_version: invitation and notice text as approved by the planner in s2, with the stakeholder list frozen at approval; any change voids it

tasks.design: Meeting materials reuse the map templates from the land use reports, and invitations are merged from one approved text to the stakeholder list and the addresses in the plan area, then sent and posted by the {WORKFLOW} platform. With participants told at the start, the meeting is recorded; a bounded step drafts the report of views by theme from the transcript and the planner's notes, each view citing a time. Written reactions are tagged by theme with quotes, but the planner reads every reaction; holding the meeting and following up stay with the planner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meeting reports were written from memory and notes, and reactions were sorted by hand in a mailbox.
tasks.enabler_now: Dutch speech-to-text makes meeting transcripts cheap; language models group free text by theme with checkable quotes.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicts between residents and developers; trust in the room.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a heated meeting fair and finding the shared interest.
tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time writing reports from memory and more on follow-up; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether themed reactions with quotes change what reaches the council.

evidence.claim: On 'most important issue' answers with 50 codes, the best language model coded 93.9% correctly against 94.7% for a second human coder.
A product groups open text answers into themes and sentiment.
Recordings and reactions contain personal data; participants must be told about recording, and reports name speakers only by role.

assumptions: Boundary: from preparing the meeting to issues followed up; the council's response to reactions is outside.
Input contract for s3: stakeholder list kept by the planner and addresses in the plan area from the municipal address register; fallback is the planner's mailing list.
Input contract for s5: a recording made with participants informed at the start; without it the planner's notes are the only input.
Coverage: about 70% of meetings are recorded; s5 is priced at that share.
The meeting itself and follow-up talks do not change; every reaction is still read.
unknowns: How many public meetings and written reactions per plan.
Whether the municipality allows recording of public meetings.
research_questions: How often does the planner change a theme the step assigned?
Do participants find their view in the report?

already_counted.description: Urban planner checks cited passages and edits the drafted meeting report.
Urban planner reads every reaction and corrects tags.

incremental.description: Urban planner informs participants about recording and handles deletion of recordings after the report.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small unrecorded meeting with few written reactions; high: a large recorded consultation with many written reactions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
